domains.label: Mathematics & optimization
domains.description: Mathematical constructions, inequalities, generic optimizers and numerical algorithms.
domains.why_it_matters: Candidate objects or algorithms can improve explicit bounds, feasibility, approximation error or search efficiency.

domains.label: Operations research
domains.description: Routing, packing, scheduling, allocation and constraint models with an operational objective.
domains.why_it_matters: These tasks study how to use limited space, time and resources under explicit constraints.

domains.label: Machine learning & language
domains.description: Learning algorithms, generic prediction, language benchmarks, retrieval and digital-agent behavior.
domains.why_it_matters: Compare generalization, reasoning, learning procedures and retrieval quality across defined data and benchmark tasks.

domains.label: Software engineering
domains.description: Program synthesis, code repair, repository tasks and verification workflows.
domains.why_it_matters: Correctness and task completion expose whether generated software satisfies a program or repository contract.

domains.label: Computer systems & hardware
domains.description: Kernels, compilers, databases, datacenters, circuits and infrastructure optimization.
domains.why_it_matters: Latency, throughput, resource use and hardware constraints connect candidate programs to computing efficiency.

domains.label: Robotics & control
domains.description: Feedback controllers, embodied policies and rewards for locomotion or manipulation.
domains.why_it_matters: Closed-loop behavior tests stability, task completion and control performance, often in simulation.

domains.label: Physics
domains.description: Physical models, cosmology, quantum systems, transport, event reconstruction and physical-law inference.
domains.why_it_matters: Compare physical constructions, inferred relationships and numerical methods against declared measurements or simulations.

domains.label: Chemistry & materials
domains.description: Reaction kinetics, chemical transformations, material properties and constitutive models.
domains.why_it_matters: Infer stress–strain relationships, integrate chemical reaction dynamics and predict reaction outcomes or material properties.

domains.label: Biology & health
domains.description: Growth, biological sequences, cellular or neural data and biological or medical prediction targets.
domains.why_it_matters: Fit growth and population models, analyze RNA and cellular data, and learn predictive relationships in biological imagery and neural activity.

domains.label: Earth & environment
domains.description: Earth-system and environmental models, observations, prediction and resource-control targets.
domains.why_it_matters: Modeling environmental observations can test forecasting or process prediction under a defined dataset protocol.

domains.label: Finance & economics
domains.description: Economic decisions, allocation, mechanism design, structural models and financial policies.
domains.why_it_matters: Study economic models and decision rules under explicit objectives, information limits and feasibility constraints.

domains.label: Mixed / unclassified
domains.description: The available metadata describes a mixed suite or does not identify one primary application domain.
domains.why_it_matters: Keep mixed or underspecified packages visible while more detailed target and evaluation evidence is recorded.

task_types.label: Mathematical construction
task_types.description: Construct a discrete or continuous object under mathematical constraints.
task_types.why_it_matters: Feasibility and an explicit extremal objective make candidate configurations directly comparable.

task_types.label: Combinatorial optimization
task_types.description: Design a constructive heuristic or search strategy for a discrete allocation problem.
task_types.why_it_matters: Solution quality and feasibility measure how a method navigates a constrained search space.

task_types.label: Black-box optimization
task_types.description: Design an optimizer, acquisition function or selection policy for an objective oracle.
task_types.why_it_matters: Evaluation budgets and attained objective values test search efficiency rather than one fixed solution.

task_types.label: Symbolic regression
task_types.description: Recover an equation, scaling law or symbolic-regression procedure from data.
task_types.why_it_matters: Held-out error tests whether a compact functional expression predicts beyond the fitted examples.

task_types.label: Numerical solver
task_types.description: Integrate or simulate specified dynamics, solve equations, or design numerical integration and sampling procedures.
task_types.why_it_matters: Accuracy and numerical cost quantify behavior on specified functions, states or trajectories.

task_types.label: Prediction & model design
task_types.description: Fit, infer, train or design a predictive or generative model, representation or parameter estimate.
task_types.why_it_matters: Prediction error or task return evaluates learned behavior on the declared data or environment.

task_types.label: Hyperparameter search
task_types.description: Optimize training settings or model hyperparameters.
task_types.why_it_matters: A held-out objective tests the quality and cost of selecting a model configuration.

task_types.label: Language & reasoning
task_types.description: Optimize prompts, scaffolds or outputs on language, reasoning or grid-inference benchmarks.
task_types.why_it_matters: Measure compositional reasoning, language understanding and constraint satisfaction on specified benchmark cases.

task_types.label: Agent workflow
task_types.description: Design an agent workflow for tools, web environments, planning or digital tasks.
task_types.why_it_matters: End-to-end task completion tests how actions and tools are coordinated across a trajectory.

task_types.label: Software generation & repair
task_types.description: Generate, repair, review or verify program code.
task_types.why_it_matters: Executable tests or repository task outcomes connect a proposed change to software behavior.

task_types.label: Systems optimization
task_types.description: Improve kernel, compiler, infrastructure, hardware or program-performance decisions.
task_types.why_it_matters: Correctness plus cost or performance measurements test whether systems changes are useful.

task_types.label: Control policy
task_types.description: Design a feedback controller, sequential decision rule or embodied action policy.
task_types.why_it_matters: Sequential outcomes test decisions under changing state and information constraints.

task_types.label: Reward design
task_types.description: Design a reward for a learning controller or policy.
task_types.why_it_matters: The resulting trained behavior tests whether the reward induces the intended task behavior.

task_types.label: Information retrieval
task_types.why_it_matters: Relevance measurements compare ranking functions and document-search quality across different collections.

task_types.label: Constraint modeling
task_types.description: Reformulate or solve explicit satisfiability, logic or mathematical-program constraints.
task_types.why_it_matters: Feasibility and solver efficiency expose the value of the model formulation or solver policy.

task_types.label: Benchmark generation
task_types.description: Generate benchmark functions or embodied evaluation tasks.
task_types.why_it_matters: Produce controlled instances for probing evaluation coverage, difficulty and optimizer or policy robustness.

task_types.label: Signal processing
task_types.description: Filter or transform a signal under error, noise and smoothness criteria.
task_types.why_it_matters: Output fidelity and robustness test whether useful signal structure survives processing.

task_types.label: Unclassified task type
task_types.description: The catalog does not yet specify a clear candidate or evaluation operation.
task_types.why_it_matters: Expose gaps in the recorded optimization contract so future catalog curation can resolve them.

coverage.label: Executable definitions
coverage.description: Packages with source-declared executable evaluators; environments and runtime are not verified by Arena.

coverage.label: Unsupported definitions
coverage.description: Catalogued packages whose source marks evaluation unsupported; they remain included in domain totals.

coverage.label: Original protocol
coverage.description: Source labels the evaluator protocol original; this is not Arena conformance or runtime verification.

coverage.label: Source-declared verified reconstruction
coverage.description: Source labels these reconstructions verified. Arena has not independently rerun that verification.

coverage.label: Recreated protocol
coverage.description: Recreated evaluators without the source's recreated_verified designation.

coverage.label: Recorded I/O contract
coverage.description: Non-null problem.json contract text; may point to evaluator documentation rather than a complete machine-readable signature.

coverage.label: Arena runtime verification recorded
coverage.description: No package in this pinned catalog carries Arena runtime verification. This does not mean its evaluator fails.

sciel-bench-arc-agi-evaluation-task-0.rationale: The candidate answers GSM8K questions or transforms ARC grids; this is capability evaluation.

evidence.description: Write two grid-transformation attempts (transform_grid_attempt_1/2 over numpy arrays) for one ARC-AGI task selected by index from the arc-prize-2025 challenge file. The pinned evaluator scores pass@2 accuracy over the task's training pairs; the source README's default is evaluation-set index 0 (task 0934a4d8).

sciel-bench-k-module-problem.rationale: The candidate searches a synthetic configuration or budgeted test function.

evidence.description: Select the correct option for each of four independent pipeline modules (loader, preprocess, algorithm, formatter; five options each, 625 combinations). The evaluator reports only how many modules are correct, so the landscape carries no per-module gradient; combined_score is the fraction of correct modules.

sciel-bench-kattis-alphabet.rationale: The candidate implements an online-judge solution or extracts an API-documentation structure.

evidence.description: Write a Python program that reads a lowercase string and prints the minimum number of letters to insert so that a..z appears as a subsequence (Kattis problem 'alphabet'). The pinned evaluator submits the candidate to open.kattis.com and reports the fraction of accepted test cases as combined_score.

sciel-bench-lm-eval-gsm8k.rationale: The candidate answers GSM8K questions or transforms ARC grids; this is capability evaluation.

evidence.description: Answer GSM8K questions through the lm-eval.py adapter, which registers an 'openevolve' model in EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness and answers each prompt by running a short evolution over a text stub. The headline metric is GSM8K exact_match (strict-match) over the evaluated examples.

sciel-bench-mlir-attention-optimization.rationale: The task changes compiler passes, an attention kernel or a sorting implementation to improve computing performance.

evidence.description: Choose MLIR pass-pipeline parameters (tile sizes, vectorization, unrolling, fusion, loop interchange) for a linalg self-attention kernel. The pinned evaluator runs mlir-opt with the chosen pipeline and estimates speedup from IR statistics; error (lower is better) penalizes shortfall from a 1.32x target.

sciel-bench-mlx-qwen3-gqa-kernel.rationale: The task changes compiler passes, an attention kernel or a sorting implementation to improve computing performance.

evidence.task_name: SCiEL: MLX Metal GQA attention kernel for Qwen3-0.6B
evidence.description: Evolve a custom Metal kernel (CustomGQAAttention) for grouped-query attention in Qwen3-0.6B-bf16 on Apple Silicon. The pinned evaluator validates the kernel, checks bfloat16 correctness against MLX's scaled_dot_product_attention and benchmarks decode/prefill throughput through mlx_lm.generate in a subprocess hook; final_score is a safety-adjusted performance score.

sciel-bench-prompt-optimization-emotion.rationale: The SCiEL package optimizes a prompt or reasoning transformation against labeled benchmark examples.

evidence.description: Evolve a text prompt for the task model on the dair-ai/emotion dataset (test split). Six-class emotion classification; accuracy over a 40-sample stage-2 slice. The pinned evaluator sends each sampled example to the configured task model and reports accuracy as combined_score.

sciel-bench-prompt-optimization-gsm8k.rationale: The SCiEL package optimizes a prompt or reasoning transformation against labeled benchmark examples.

evidence.description: Evolve a text prompt for the task model on the openai/gsm8k (main) dataset (test split). Grade-school math word problems; the numeric answer after #### is compared. The pinned evaluator sends each sampled example to the configured task model and reports accuracy as combined_score.

sciel-bench-prompt-optimization-hotpotqa.rationale: The SCiEL package optimizes a prompt or reasoning transformation against labeled benchmark examples.

Among integer polynomials of degree at most 12 the least measure above one is Lehmer's number, so the task recovers Lehmer's polynomial (up to sign, reversal and cyclotomic factors).

evidence.description: Return [start,length] for a nonempty interval contained in [1,1008]. For EVERY x,y in the interval, including x=y, require x*y %1009 !=1. Maximize interval length. Finite obstruction search for the modular inverse-pair interval question. Diagonal pairs are checked, so the self-inverse residues1 and1008 cannot be present; this is stricter than the preliminary distinct-pair proposal.

science-number-theory-lcm-reciprocal-wei.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large reciprocal weight under lcm separation" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Large reciprocal weight under lcm separation
evidence.description: Return nonempty subset of [2,256] with lcm(a,b)>256 for all distinct pairs. Maximize exact reciprocal sum, not cardinality. Uses the reciprocal-sum objective in section14(1), with n fixed; pairwise lcm threshold is strict and the score is rational. The unit denominator1 is excluded locally to remove its isolated trivial certificate.

science-number-theory-noncoprime-forced.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large pairwise noncoprime sets containing the interval endpoint" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Large pairwise noncoprime sets containing the interval endpoint
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,255] containing 255, with gcd(a,b)>1 for all distinct pairs. Maximize cardinality. Fixes n=255 in g(n), the source's exact forced-maximum-element formulation; no solution to a general coprime-family conjecture is claimed.

science-number-theory-pair-sum-nondivisi.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Integer sets whose pair sums never divide pair products" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Integer sets whose pair sums never divide pair products
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,256]. For every distinct a,b require (a*b)%(a+b)!=0. Maximize cardinality. The prescribed distinct-pair divisibility exclusion does not require the quotient to belong to the selected set, unlike the reciprocal Schur task. The source writes x,y without explicitly excluding equality; this implementation follows the bank's stated distinct-pair variant.

science-number-theory-power-residue-run.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Early runs of five quadratic residues modulo1009" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Early runs of five quadratic residues modulo1009
evidence.description: Return {'start':s,'roots':[r0,...,r4]}, with 1<=s<=1004 and 1<=ri<=1008. Require ri**2 mod 1009 == s+i. Minimize s; zero residues and wraparound are excluded. A fixed-prime instance of the least run-start r(k,m,p), with k=2 and m=5. Each residue is certified by its root; no limsup over primes is computed.

science-number-theory-powerful-consecuti.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Consecutive powerful non-squares: exact counterexample certificate" (Prize-listed mathematical problems); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Consecutive powerful non-squares: exact counterexample certificate
evidence.description: Provide a positive integer n and complete prime factorizations certifying that n and n+1 are powerful and neither is a square. Every prime exponent must be at least two. The verifier uses exact integers and primality tests. This recreates the resolved yes/no question in JSP-000301, with a local certificate-size bound n+1 <= 10^12 and binary validity score. The published 12167/12168 witness is explicitly credited to Solomon W. Golomb.

science-number-theory-powerful-parts.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large powerful-part product for consecutive integers" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Large powerful-part product for consecutive integers
evidence.description: Return an integer n in [10000,1000000]. Its powerful part is the product of FULL prime powers p^e with exponent e>=2 in its factorization. Maximize powerful_part(n)*powerful_part(n+1). The B2 powerful-part construction allows squarefree factors and does not require either whole integer to be powerful or nonsquare; distinct from the existing Golomb counterexample certificate.

science-number-theory-reciprocal-schur-f.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large sets avoiding reciprocal Schur triples" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Large sets avoiding reciprocal Schur triples
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,180] with no THREE DISTINCT elements a,b,c satisfying 1/a=1/b+1/c. Maximize cardinality. Three-distinct-element specialization of the reciprocal equation, weaker than forbidding arbitrary reciprocal subsums.

science-number-theory-reciprocal-subset-.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large reciprocal-subsum-free sets" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,24]; no reciprocal of a selected element may equal the sum of reciprocals of a subset of the OTHER selected elements. Maximize cardinality. Finite version of the extremal S* question; operands are distinct selected elements and the target is excluded from its own subsum.

science-number-theory-sidon-obstruction.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Ambient integer sets with small largest Sidon subset" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Ambient integer sets with small largest Sidon subset
evidence.description: Return exactly 12 distinct integers in [0,128]. Evaluator exhaustively computes the largest subset with all unordered pair sums unique INCLUDING diagonals. MINIMIZE that maximum subset size. The candidate chooses a hard AMBIENT set; the evaluator solves Sidon extraction exactly. This reverses the outer optimization compared with constructing a large Sidon set in a fixed interval.

science-number-theory-signed-harmonic.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Small nonzero signed harmonic subsums" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.description: Return exactly 30 integer coefficients from {-1,0,1}. The signed sum coefficient[i-1]/i must be nonzero. Minimize its absolute value; exact numerator and denominator are reported. Finite signed-harmonic extremum with the zero sum excluded; no asymptotic separation claim.

science-number-theory-smooth-adjacent.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Small largest prime factor of consecutive-integer products" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Small largest prime factor of consecutive-integer products
evidence.description: Return integer n in [10000,1000000]. Minimize the largest prime factor of n(n+1), independently computed by exact trial division. Searches a bounded window for smooth consecutive integers. The local lower cutoff prevents the trivial pair1,2; it proves no asymptotic bound.

science-number-theory-smooth-decompositi.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Smooth two-summand decomposition of a prescribed integer" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Smooth two-summand decomposition of a prescribed integer
evidence.description: Return two positive integers a,b with a+b=123457. Minimize max(P(a),P(b)), where P is the largest prime factor and P(1)=1. The evaluator factors both integers independently. One fixed-target version of the small-prime-factor additive decomposition question; no universal bound for all large integers is asserted.

science-number-theory-smooth-parts.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Few distinct small-prime parts in a short integer interval" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Few distinct small-prime parts in a short integer interval
evidence.description: Return n in [1000,1000000]. For each n+i,1<=i<=24, extract its complete factor composed of primes STRICTLY BELOW 24. MINIMIZE the number of distinct extracted factors. Uses the source minimum f(n,t) at t=24, correcting the preliminary feasibility proposal's reversed direction; the source asks for a uniform lower bound on this minimum.

science-number-theory-square-sum-free.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Integer sets avoiding square pair sums, including diagonals" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Integer sets avoiding square pair sums, including diagonals
evidence.description: Return nonempty subset of [1,256] such that a+b is never a perfect square for a<=b in the set, INCLUDING a=b. Maximize cardinality. Explicit diagonal-including restriction resolves the terse bank wording; all pairs are verified with integer square roots. It is distinct from square DIFFERENCE avoidance.

science-number-theory-target-subsum-free.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large interval sets avoiding a prescribed subset sum" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Large interval sets avoiding a prescribed subset sum
evidence.description: Return a nonempty subset of [1,100] with no subset summing to 200. Maximize cardinality. Each element can occur at most once in the forbidden sum. Fixes the target and ambient interval in the question about integers below n/k avoiding a subset sum n; the inclusive endpoint convention is local.

science-number-theory-totient-multiple.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Small integer whose totient is divisible by 120" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Small integer whose totient is divisible by 120
evidence.description: Return integer n in [1,1000000] with phi(n) divisible by 120. Minimize n; the evaluator independently factors n and computes the exact totient. Constructs m_n from the source by fixing its divisor parameter to120; does not compare asymptotic ratios with least primes in progressions.

science-number-theory-unique-block-produ.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Dense increasing sequences with unique block products" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Dense increasing sequences with unique block products
evidence.description: Return strictly increasing integers in [2,128]. Products of every nonempty consecutive block must be distinct. Maximize length; singleton products are included. Finite restriction of the density-one sequence question. The implementation neither verifies nor relies on the bank's unverified modern solution/priority claims.

science-number-theory-unique-interval-su.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Increasing sequences with unique consecutive-block sums" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Increasing sequences with unique consecutive-block sums
evidence.description: Return a strictly increasing sequence of integers in [1,256]. Sums of all nonempty consecutive blocks must be distinct. Maximize sequence length. Finite version of the Erdős–Harzheim increasing-sequence question. Only consecutive blocks, not arbitrary subsets, must have distinct sums.

science-number-theory-unit-fraction-pack.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Closest strict underpacking of one by supplied unit fractions" (Problem-bank constructions: arithmetic and extremal sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Closest strict underpacking of one by supplied unit fractions
evidence.description: Return nonempty distinct zero-based indices into denominators [2,3,...,48]; reciprocal sum must be STRICTLY BELOW 1. Minimize positive deficit 1-sum; exact rational value is reported. Fixed finite input collection whose reciprocal total exceeds one; minimizes the strict deficit rather than asserting a uniform bound for all collections. The source permits an exact-one subsum; the local protocol explicitly excludes it.

science-odd-covering-divisors-of-51975.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Odd covering systems with moduli dividing 51975 (fewest uncovered residues)" (Problem-bank constructions: number theory and additive sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Odd covering systems with moduli dividing 51975 (fewest uncovered residues)
evidence.description: construct() -> classes [[m, r], ...] with distinct moduli m > 1 dividing 51975 = 3^3 * 5^2 * 7 * 11 (hence odd) and 0 <= r < m. The score is the number of residues modulo 51975 covered by no class (exact). Minimize; 0 would be a covering system with distinct odd moduli. With every divisor of 51975 available once, a score of 0 would exhibit an odd covering; positive scores measure how close systems with this modulus come. No minimum is documented.

science-one-repeated-sum-100.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Subsets of {1, ..., 100} in which at most one sum is repeated" (Problem-bank constructions: number theory and additive sets); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Subsets of {1, ..., 100} in which at most one sum is repeated
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..100 such that at most one integer has more than one representation a + b with a <= b in the set. Maximize the size; the optimum is 16. For N = 100 the maximum is 16, so the task recovers an extremal set.

science-oppositely-ordered-farey-pair-10.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Nearby oppositely ordered fractions in the Farey sequence" (Problem-bank constructions: geometry and discrete structures); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Nearby oppositely ordered fractions in the Farey sequence
evidence.description: construct() -> [[a,b],[c,d]], two reduced fractions in [0,1] with denominators <=1000, a/b<c/d, and (c-a)*(d-b)<0. Minimize their rank difference in the complete Farey sequence of order 1000, including 0/1 and 1/1. Every rank is recomputed exactly. The local finite search gives an upper certificate for the first possible ordering failure at order 1000. It corrects the feasibility draft's unrelated strictly monotone-run objective. The optimum is 252, found by scanning the complete Farey sequence of order 1000; this is a rediscovery task.

science-orchard-twelve-rational-points.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Twelve rational points with many three-point lines (orchard problem)" (Problem-bank constructions: discrete geometry and analysis); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Twelve rational points with many three-point lines (orchard problem)
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 12 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^30 (any rational configuration can be scaled to integers). Maximize the number of lines containing exactly three of the points, computed exactly; the optimum is 19. The real maximum for 12 points is 19, and the group law on a rational cubic with 12-torsion realizes it with rational points, so the rational optimum is also 19.

science-ordinary-lines-twelve-rational-p.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Twelve rational points with few ordinary lines" (Problem-bank constructions: discrete geometry and analysis); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Twelve rational points with few ordinary lines
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 12 distinct integer points [x, y] with |x|, |y| <= 10^9, not all collinear. Minimize the number of lines containing exactly two of the points (exact). Over the reals the minimum for 12 points is 6; whether integer (rational) coordinates reach 6 is not documented, so scores are compared with that lower bound.

science-pair-sum-prime-diversity-12.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Few prime factors across pairwise sums" (Problem-bank constructions: additive combinatorics); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Few prime factors across pairwise sums
evidence.description: construct() -> n=12 distinct positive integers <=maximum=10000. Factor every sum of two DISTINCT elements, union all prime factors and minimize the number of distinct primes. Choose 12 distinct positive integers at most 10000; minimize the number of distinct primes dividing sums of distinct-index pairs. Equal-index sums are excluded.

science-paired-sidon-disjoint-difference.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Two Sidon sets with disjoint difference sets" (Problem-bank constructions: additive combinatorics); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Two Sidon sets with disjoint difference sets
evidence.description: construct() -> [A,B], two nonempty Sidon subsets of [1,n=256], at most 64 elements each. Pair sums inside each set, including a+a, must be unique. Their nonzero difference sets must be disjoint. Maximize |A|+|B|; A and B need not themselves be disjoint. Two Sidon subsets of [1,256]; maximize combined size and require disjoint nonzero differences. Ordinary Sidon diagonals are included, and the two sets themselves may overlap.

science-pairwise-sum-triple-free-sets.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Large sets without a triple and all its pair sums" (Problem-bank constructions: graphs and set systems); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Large sets without a triple and all its pair sums
evidence.description: construct() -> distinct integers in 1..128. Forbid THREE DISTINCT members a,b,c for which a+b, a+c and b+c are also selected. The six displayed values need not be mutually distinct. Maximize set size. The local interval ends at 128. The evaluator uses only exact finite checks and does not assume the preprint’s proof, novelty, status, or Lean verification. The baseline is the elementary upper half interval.

science-pancyclic-graph-excess-40.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Sparse pancyclic graphs on 40 vertices" (Problem-bank constructions: geometry and discrete structures); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.description: construct() -> {'edges': undirected edge pairs on vertices 0..39, 'cycles': one vertex-list cycle of every length 3..40 in that order}. Edges are simple and distinct; cycle vertices are distinct and every required edge must exist. Minimize edge count minus 40. This is an independently implemented n=40 construction search with explicit cycle certificates. The seed is an elementary fan graph, not a copied minimal construction.

science-penny-graph-contacts-32.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Contact numbers of 32 unit pennies on the triangular lattice" (Problem-bank constructions: discrete geometry and analysis); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Contact numbers of 32 unit pennies on the triangular lattice
evidence.description: construct() -> exactly 32 distinct integer pairs [a, b] with |a|, |b| <= 64 denoting lattice points a + b*omega, omega = exp(i*pi/3), which are at mutual distance at least one. Maximize the number of pairs at distance exactly one; Harborth's theorem gives the optimum floor(3n - sqrt(12n - 3)) = 76. Harborth's formula gives 76 for n = 32 and triangular-lattice spirals attain it, so the lattice restriction loses nothing.

science-pentagon-hexagon-free-extremal-4.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Graphs on 42 vertices without five- or six-cycles" (Problem-bank constructions: extremal graphs, hypergraphs and designs); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Graphs on 42 vertices without five- or six-cycles
evidence.description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple graph on vertices 0..41 containing neither a five-cycle nor a six-cycle. Maximize the number of edges; the known optimum is 104. The exact value 104 for n = 42 is known; the task recovers it.

science-permutation-monotone-progression.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Permutations avoiding long monotone progressions" (Problem-bank constructions: additive combinatorics); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.description: construct() -> a permutation of 1..n=128. Minimize the longest subsequence whose values form an increasing OR decreasing nonconstant arithmetic progression; subsequence positions need not be adjacent. A known finite construction attains 2, so this is a rediscovery task. Permute [1,128] and minimize the longest arithmetic-progression subsequence, allowing either sign of the common difference. The known finite optimum is 2; infinite-permutation questions are not recreated here.

science-physics-freegsnke-coil-design.rationale: The candidate constructs bounded coil-current settings for a specified plasma boundary; this is physical configuration design, not a robot policy. Reviewed source family science_physics_freegsnke_coil_design, area physics.

science-physics-mlgwsc-event-search.rationale: The candidate detects and ranks events in gravitational-wave strain signals under a false-alarm constraint. Reviewed source family science_physics_mlgwsc_event_search, area cosmology_and_astrophysics.

evidence.description: pulse(target_gate, hardware_model) -> (80,2) IQ amplitudes rad/ns for 40 ns X-pi gate in a three-level Duffing transmon. Enforce amplitude .4 rad/ns and slew .12 rad/ns/ns including endpoints. Independent Lindblad expm and refined DOP853 evaluate six Bloch states over 3x3 detuning/calibration cases, relaxation and dephasing. Score mean plus worst average gate infidelity; report leakage. Explicit simulation, not QuOCS benchmark reproduction.

science-physics-tdlmc-distance-posterior.rationale: The source specifies physical-event reconstruction, a physical surrogate, decoding, imaging or parameter inference. Fixed-work local adaptation, not a timing leaderboard.

science-planar-bipartite-list-colouring.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Colouring four fixed planar bipartite graphs from lists of three colours" (Problem-bank constructions: hypergraphs, graph constructions and instance-solving methods); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Colouring four fixed planar bipartite graphs from lists of three colours
evidence.description: construct() -> four colourings, one per instance from planar_bipartite_lists(splits, seed) for (20,701), (40,702), (60,703), (100,704) in the verifier: a bipartite quadrangulation grown from the cube by inserting squares into random faces (minimum degree 3), with a random list of 3 colours from 0..4 per vertex. Each vertex must take a colour from its list and adjacent vertices must differ. The score is the number of properly coloured instances (0..4). Maximize; all are colourable by the Alon-Tarsi theorem. The score counts fixed instances coloured properly from their lists; it measures a constructive list-colouring method for a theorem proved non-constructively.

science-point-sets-without-empty-hexagon.rationale: Construct a finite object for "Point sets without an empty convex hexagon (rediscovering 29 points)" (Problem-bank constructions: discrete geometry and analysis); the local verifier checks the stated constraints and scores the construction.

evidence.task_name: Point sets without an empty convex hexagon (rediscovering 29 points)

methodology.classification_authority: Arena editorial inference from the pinned catalog; these labels are not a taxonomy supplied or certified by the source authors.
methodology.unit: One canonical registered task package (task ID). This snapshot merges 253 upstream aliases; remaining parameter variants and distinct protocols are separate packages. Counts are not counts of unique scientific problems.
methodology.primary_domain: Exactly one primary application domain per package. Classification follows the candidate objective/target, not paper-title keywords or the subject of QA/retrieval documents. Cross-domain connections are discussed in definitions, never counted twice.
methodology.task_type: Exactly one task type per package, describing the candidate operation independently of application domain.
methodology.rules: Ordered first-match rules: explicit scientific targets and mixed-family exceptions, reviewed task groups, defaults for each of 357 source families, then unknown. Conditions within a rule are AND; values within one condition are OR. Historical rule IDs containing unsupported do not override current catalog availability.
methodology.evidence: Annotations retain the matched rule, rationale, task name, description, metric, source family and paper IDs. Exact-ID lists were resolved using catalog/duplicates.json at source commit 5729caa7a3bd4e66c39a447c0d4ee56dc8fa0935; merged predecessors had consistent domain/type assignments. New family classifications review catalog/tasks.json, labels.area, candidate interfaces and catalog/science/*.json at that commit. Tasks imported later from source commit a5e50ed6355b14e0a09e98a1afeba8e4e4c9b1fd (the prize-bank collections and the MCTS-AHD admissible-set task restored after an incorrect duplicate merge) were classified from catalog/science/prize*.json, labels.area and their candidate contracts at that commit. These are editorial classifications, not endorsements of upstream scientific-importance or open-problem labels.
methodology.percentages: Each domain distribution and each task-type distribution uses all catalog packages as denominator. Largest-remainder rounding to 0.1 percentage point makes each partition sum to 100.0%; ties use taxonomy definition order.
methodology.availability: Executable and unsupported counts preserve source protocol status. Classification neither installs an environment nor establishes runtime readiness, fidelity, reproducibility or Arena conformance.
methodology.papers: Corpus paper counts exclude the 25 supplemental source IDs declared in non_paper_source_ids: SCiEL, Santa 2025 and 23 science collections. This snapshot covers 98 corpus paper IDs and 123 source groups. unique_paper_count is a compatibility alias for source_group_count; label it source groups. Per-group paper_count counts corpus IDs, not independently verified publications. Per-group source_group_count includes supplements; group coverage overlaps.
methodology.families: Family counts exclude null source families. Families can span domains/types and must not be summed across groups.
methodology.coverage: Coverage rows are overlapping indicators, each using the complete package denominator. They are not a distribution and their percentages must not be summed.
methodology.scientific_relevance: why_it_matters describes the modeled function or evaluation operation, not a subjective scientific-importance ranking or a claim that the benchmark produced a discovery.
methodology.refresh: Changing catalog or taxonomy requires rebuilding insights.json. Offline validation compares digests, every assignment and all aggregate totals before serving the Python API.
